stages.name: Other states
stages.desc: Ptolemaic lands, Macedon, Greek leagues and other powers outside both camps

stages.name: Carthage
stages.desc: Independent, but disarmed and bound by the peace treaty of 201 BC

stages.name: Rome and its allies
stages.desc: Rome, its Italian and Greek allies, Pergamon and Rhodes

stages.name: Seleucid realm
stages.desc: The empire of Antiochus III, from Asia Minor to Mesopotamia

stages.name: Kingdoms sheltering Hannibal
stages.desc: Rulers who took the fugitive in after Antiochus' defeat

stages.name: Hannibal's current location
stages.desc: Where Hannibal was in that year

states.name: Israel
timeline: Ptolemaic Coele-Syria
Antiochus defeats the Ptolemaic army at Panium and takes Coele-Syria

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Ptolemaic Coele-Syria: Judaea and the coastal plain
Judaea passes to the Seleucids after Panium

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Ptolemaic Phoenicia: Tyre, Sidon and Byblos
Antiochus wins Phoenicia from Egypt at Panium
Hannibal lands at Tyre, Carthage's mother city
Phoenician cities build ships for Antiochus

states.name: Syria
timeline: The Seleucid heartland: Apamea, Seleucia Pieria and the Phoenician isle of Aradus
Hannibal raises a war fleet from the Phoenician cities
Defeated, Antiochus keeps Syria, the core of his realm

states.name: North Macedonia
timeline: Part of Philip V's kingdom of Macedon
Philip is crushed at Cynoscephalae and bound by treaty to Rome
Philip V fights on Rome's side against Antiochus

states.name: Albania
timeline: Illyrian coast under Roman protection: Apollonia, Epidamnus and allied chiefs
Flamininus defeats Philip at the Aous gorge

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Seleucid Sardis and Antioch dominate; Pergamon, Bithynia and Rhodes stay independent
Antiochus seizes the coastal cities of Cilicia, Lycia and Ionia
Hannibal reaches Antiochus at Ephesus and becomes his adviser
Hannibal follows Antiochus' army to Greece
Back at Ephesus after Thermopylae, Hannibal prepares a fleet
Hannibal's fleet is beaten off Side by the Rhodians; Antiochus loses at Magnesia
The peace terms at Sardis demand Hannibal's surrender; he escapes
Peace of Apamea: the Seleucids leave Asia Minor to Pergamon and Rhodes
Prusias I of Bithynia takes Hannibal in and gives him command against Pergamon
Hannibal beats Eumenes' fleet by hurling pots of snakes onto its decks
Rome demands his surrender; at Libyssa, Hannibal takes poison

states.name: Armenia
timeline: Armenia, governed for Antiochus by the strategoi Artaxias and Zariadris
Debated: Artaxias, now king, shelters Hannibal, who is said to plan Artaxata
Independent Armenia under Artaxias I

states.name: Libya
timeline: Carthage's Emporia, the rich coastal towns around Leptis; Cyrenaica is Ptolemaic
Masinissa of Numidia raids the Emporia; Rome leaves the dispute unresolved

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Hannibal is defeated at Zama; Carthage sues for peace
Peace: Carthage gives up its fleet and owes Rome 10,000 talents over fifty years
Hannibal is elected suffete and breaks the power of the Hundred and Four
Denounced to Rome by his enemies, Hannibal flees by night
Carthage offers to pay off the rest of its indemnity at once; Rome refuses

states.name: Greece
timeline: Philip V's Macedon, the Aetolian and Achaean leagues, free cities and Rhodes
Flamininus proclaims the freedom of the Greeks under Roman protection
Invited by the Aetolians, Antiochus lands at Demetrias and takes Chalcis
The Romans rout Antiochus at Thermopylae; he and Hannibal retreat to Asia
Debated: Nepos and Justin say Hannibal hid on Crete, at Gortyn
Greece under Roman influence; Rhodes enlarged by the peace of Apamea

states.name: Iraq
timeline: Babylonia, ruled from Seleucia on the Tigris

states.name: Italy
timeline: Rome and its Italian allies, victorious in the Second Punic War
Rome declares war on Philip V of Macedon
Rome declares war on Antiochus III
Scipio Africanus dies in retirement at Liternum

states.name: Jordan
timeline: Ptolemaic lands east of the Jordan
Passes to the Seleucids after Panium

states.name: Malta
timeline: Malta, once Carthaginian, held by Rome since 218 BC

events.title: Battle of Zama
events.text: Scipio defeats Hannibal in North Africa, ending the Second Punic War.

events.title: Hannibal at Hadrumetum
events.text: Hannibal escapes the battlefield to his base at Hadrumetum and urges Carthage to accept peace.

events.title: Peace with Rome
events.text: Carthage surrenders its warships and elephants and agrees to pay 10,000 talents over fifty years.

events.title: Battle of Panium
events.text: Antiochus III defeats the Ptolemaic army and wins Coele-Syria and Phoenicia.

events.title: War on Macedon
events.text: Rome declares war on Philip V, Hannibal's former ally.

events.title: Battle of the Aous
events.text: Flamininus forces Philip's army out of the Aous gorge.

events.title: Cynoscephalae
events.text: The Roman legions crush the Macedonian phalanx in Thessaly.

events.title: Antiochus sails west
events.text: Antiochus' fleet takes the coastal cities of Cilicia, Lycia and Ionia.

events.title: Hannibal elected suffete
events.text: Hannibal becomes chief magistrate of Carthage.

events.title: The Hundred and Four
events.text: Hannibal makes the oligarchs' judges' council elected yearly, and audits the treasury.

events.title: Freedom of the Greeks
events.text: At the Isthmian Games, Flamininus proclaims the Greek cities free.

events.title: Lysimachia
events.text: Antiochus crosses into Europe and rebuilds Lysimachia; Roman envoys warn him off.

events.title: Rome's envoys
events.text: A Roman embassy arrives at Carthage; Hannibal's enemies have accused him of plotting with Antiochus.

events.title: Flight by night
events.text: Hannibal rides to his coastal estate near Thapsus and sails away in secret.

events.title: Cercina
events.text: On the island of Cercina he throws a feast so no ship can leave to report him.

events.title: Landing at Tyre
events.text: Hannibal is welcomed in Tyre, the Phoenician mother city of Carthage.

events.title: Meeting Antiochus
events.text: Hannibal joins the king at Ephesus, the Seleucid base in the west.

events.title: Rome leaves Greece
events.text: Flamininus withdraws the legions from Greece.

events.title: Masinissa's raid
events.text: Numidian horsemen raid Carthage's Emporia; Rome declines to decide the dispute.

events.title: Aristo of Tyre
events.text: Hannibal's agent stirs his partisans at Carthage, then slips away.

events.title: Scipio at Ephesus
events.text: Debated: Livy reports that Scipio met Hannibal and asked him who was the greatest general.

events.title: A royal marriage
events.text: Antiochus marries his daughter Cleopatra to Ptolemy V at Raphia.

events.title: Antiochus in Greece
events.text: Invited by the Aetolians, Antiochus lands at Demetrias with ten thousand men.

events.title: Winter at Chalcis
events.text: Antiochus holds court at Chalcis; Hannibal urges a war in Italy.

events.title: Thermopylae
events.text: Manius Acilius Glabrio routs Antiochus at the famous pass.

events.title: Battle of Corycus
events.text: The Roman and Pergamene fleets defeat Antiochus' admiral Polyxenidas.

events.title: Carthage's offer
events.text: Carthage offers to pay its remaining indemnity at once; Rome refuses.

events.title: Fleet from Phoenicia
events.text: Hannibal raises a new fleet from Aradus, Sidon and Tyre.

events.title: Battle of Side
events.text: Off the Eurymedon, the Rhodians under Eudamus defeat Hannibal's fleet.

events.title: Myonessus
events.text: The Roman and Rhodian fleets destroy Polyxenidas' fleet; the sea is lost.

events.title: Battle of Magnesia
events.text: In the winter of 190–189 the Scipio brothers crush Antiochus' army.

events.title: Terms at Sardis
events.text: Rome's peace terms demand that Antiochus hand over Hannibal.

events.title: Gortyn
events.text: Debated: Hannibal hides on Crete, guarding his gold in jars said to hold lead.

events.title: Peace of Apamea
events.text: Antiochus gives up Asia Minor west of the Taurus and his fleet and elephants.

events.title: Artaxata
events.text: Debated: Strabo and Plutarch say Hannibal chose the site of Armenia's new capital.

events.title: Bithynia
events.text: Prusias I gives Hannibal refuge and a command in his war with Pergamon.

events.title: Prusa
events.text: Debated: Pliny says Prusias founded Prusa on Hannibal's advice.

events.title: Pots of snakes
events.text: Hannibal wins a sea fight against Eumenes II by throwing jars of snakes onto his ships.

events.title: Flamininus' demand
events.text: Titus Flamininus asks Prusias to surrender Hannibal.

events.title: Death at Libyssa
events.text: Surrounded, Hannibal takes poison rather than fall into Roman hands.

events.title: Scipio dies
events.text: Hannibal's conqueror dies the same year, embittered, at Liternum.

events.title: Philopoemen dies
events.text: The Achaean general is poisoned at Messene: three great generals die in one year.

chartNote: Share of the area of fifteen present-day countries, by the power that dominated most of each; regions are today's boundaries. A simplification: Turkey held Seleucid, Pergamene, Rhodian and Bithynian lands at once, and Libya's vast desert counts with Carthage's coastal Emporia. Hannibal's location marks the country he was in that year; episodes in Crete and Armenia are debated.
